native_name: 三菱重工業株式会社 (Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Ltd.)

selection.reason: Japan's broadest defence manufacturer (Type 90 and Type 10 tanks, the F-2 support fighter, H-IIA launch vehicles, Taigei-class submarines and Mogami-class frigates) with civilian shipbuilding and power businesses. Japan's only supplier programme in the game is an aircraft slot, so researching MHI prevents a duplicate Japanese aircraft or armour exporter.

A code comment names Mitsubishi's J/APG-1 radar. Its maker was not researched here and it is not attached to MHI.

summary: The present MHI was formed in 1964 by the merger of three successor companies and kept its name through the window. Mass production of the Type 90 tank began in 1991 and of the Type 10 in 2011; the F-2 first flew in 1995, was first delivered in 2000 and last delivered in 2011. MHI ran H-IIA launches from Flight 13 (2007) to the final Flight 50 (29 June 2025). It formed Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems with Hitachi in 2014, renamed it Mitsubishi Power in 2020 and absorbed its thermal power business in 2021. SpaceJet development by its subsidiary Mitsubishi Aircraft was discontinued in 2023. Taigei (2022) and Mogami (2022) were delivered to the Ministry of Defense; an Australian contract for three upgraded Mogami-class frigates (April 2026) is announced only.

proposed.uncertainty: A generic main-battle-tank envelope, not a Type 90 or Type 10 replica; components and performance stay the commissioning country's design.
The F-2 is a "support fighter" derived from the F-16 and developed jointly with the US; the game strike airframe has no interception role, so the air-defence half of the type is not represented.

Japan's only supplier programme is a modeled light-attack exporter created at runtime, not a historical firm. The F-2 is a larger support fighter and no Japanese light-attack type was researched; attaching a real identity needs a ruling so that Japan does not gain two aircraft exporters.
Arsenal kits are generic capability tiers with no company stock; the Type 90 informs flavour only.
Generic escort tier; kits have no company stock or shipyard ownership.
Generated contractors are fictional; a real identity would replace one generated defense contractor, not add a parallel firm.
MHI builds thermal power systems (Mitsubishi Power until 2021); energy contractors improve funded energy-facility work, which is only loosely the same activity.

duplicates_avoided: Mitsubishi Motors (automobile division independent since 1970) is a separate company; it is the Renault-Nissan alliance member named in fr_renault, not MHI.
Mitsubishi Electric and other Mitsubishi-named companies are not merged into this dossier; the J/APG-1 radar comment in the game code is not attributed to MHI.
Taigei-class boats are attributed hull by hull: Taigei to MHI, Hakugei to Kawasaki Heavy Industries.
Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems and Mitsubishi Power are one legal person under two names; Hitachi is recorded only as a joint-venture partner.

integration_flow.summary: A later, reviewed integration could attach this sourced identity to a company created through the existing orders. Design stays with the commissioning country; Defense R&D pays development as work is performed; the company funds tooling, national-warehouse inputs and fabrication from its own settled cash; the buyer purchases whole finished units from company stock; delivery follows fiscal settlement and seven accessible days. No company order builds launch vehicles, airliners or civilian ships; an export such as the Australian frigate would use the existing ImportPurchase route from company stock, never a scripted contract.

steps.note: Paid capitalisation from Defense procurement (political capital price applies); leases one existing completed Arms Plant slot. No historical factory, balance or stock is granted.
Further paid working capital; unsettled receivables are not spendable cash.
Frozen design revision; Defense R&D pays engineering, prototype and trials work day by day; prototypes are never saleable.
Finite company-owned stock target (0-12 units); a target is never a government order.
Government buys whole units from existing company stock; settlement then seven accessible delivery days.

unmapped: H-IIA and H3 launch vehicles: no space-launch product consumer.
Taigei-class submarine: the only submarine kit (aip_ssk) assumes air-independent propulsion, while MHI describes the class as diesel-electric with lithium-ion batteries.
SpaceJet regional jet (cancelled) and Crystal Harmony cruise ship: no civilian aircraft or shipbuilding consumer.
Thermal power systems: no power-equipment product consumer beyond sector contractors.

gaps: No official dated milestone was captured for the Type 16 maneuver combat vehicle or the Soryu class; MHI product pages list them without dates.
The MHI/Hitachi shareholding in Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems (2014-2020) is known only from a lead.
The fate of Mitsubishi Aircraft Corporation after February 2023 is reported only by news.
JMSDF naming and launch pages were blocked by a bot challenge and are recorded as inaccessible.
The GCAP next-generation fighter was not researched.

future_policy.note: Nothing after the frozen cutoff is predicted. Any later product, successor or business in a campaign must be authored as explicitly fictional game content (labelled "(fictional)") or left unknown.
